title: Use versioned, structured, fail-closed envelopes for machine exchange
summary: When bash hands structured data to a tool or another component, the answer must be: a single parseable document on stdout, schema-versioned so old shapes are not silently reshaped, with real errors as typed objects that carry a code — and any ambiguity or malformed input fails closed (denies) rather than proceeding on an assumption.
technique: Versioned schema names at the head of a JSON envelope; a typed error object with ok:false, a reason and a numeric rc nested, not a human string; and a default posture that an unknown operation, unparseable JSON, or missing answer denies instead of trying to interpret. In protocol mode nothing human is printed on stdout.
evidence_note: docs/QUEUE_DEV_CONTRACT.md:72 'The JSON schema names are intentionally versioned...'; QUEUE_COMMAND_CONTRACT.md:56-67 shows a queuebash.error.v1 envelope carrying rc; :8-9 broker keeps stdout for protocol; REMOTE_QUEUE_SERVICE_PROVIDER.md:56 lists fail-closed denial on unparseable JSON/unknown/unsafe; CLOUD_INFRASTRUCTURE_HELPERS.md gives dry_run-by-default action envelopes with an explicit live gate.
invariants: Head every wire document with a versioned schema identity; a breaking change is a new schema name.
Model failures as structured typed objects carrying a code, not by string-mangling diagnostics.
Keep stdout in protocol mode strictly for the document; route diagnostics to stderr/audit.
Deny on ambiguous or malformed input rather than guessing intent, and fail closed when a component or answer is absent.
Prefer dry-run by default and add mutation only behind an explicit, separate gate from credentials.
